gap_notes: CORE cannot be scored yet: ingested sources are still classical only (Ptolemy, Lilly, Valens). Psychological, living-traditional, and professional schools pending.

Valens I.1 is a topical/significator catalog (sect, colour, taste, body parts), not Ptolemy/Lilly elemental qualities. Do not backfill heat/cold/dry/moist from Valens, and do not average catalogs into function.

Valens I.1 attests convertibility (effects vary with zodiac and other stars) without a native cold/dry quality. Native-quality conflict (Ptolemy alternate dry/moist vs Lilly melancholy) is not resolved.

Native-quality conflict: Ptolemy makes Mercury alternate dryness and moisture with equal vigour; Lilly says of his own nature he is cold and dry / melancholy, then takes the planet he joins. Do not collapse to one elemental lemma.
Corpus has no dedicated psychological title for Mercury. Do not invent a Greene-Mercury locus.
Object-level themes mix compared and school_specific lemmas. Per-lemma evidence_tier stays in this ledger; knowledge-object schema is not expanded for that.
Layer 1 requires positive_expression; it is filled from Lilly well-dignified manners only until a second school class is compared. Valens is still source_class=classical.

claims.author: Claudius Ptolemy / J.M. Ashmand trans.
claims.locus: Tetrabiblos Book I Chapter V (Ashmand p.14)
claims.original_claim: Mercury is of common influence, good or evil in unison with whatever planets he is connected with.
claims.normalized_claim: Mercury takes colour from what it joins

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XIII Nature (1659 p.76–77)
claims.original_claim: With the good he is good, with the evil planets ill; he is masculine or feminine as joined to any planet.
claims.normalized_claim: Mercury takes colour from what it joins

claims.author: Claudius Ptolemy / J.M. Ashmand trans.
claims.locus: Tetrabiblos Book I Chapter IV (Ashmand p.14)
claims.original_claim: Excited by velocity of motion with the Sun, Mercury operates rapid changes of dryness and moisture.
claims.normalized_claim: Mercury's tempo is fast and changeable

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XIII Colour and Motion (1659 p.76)
claims.original_claim: Mercury is sometimes so swift he moves more than a degree in a day; never more than about 1°40'.
claims.normalized_claim: Mercury's tempo is fast and changeable

claims.author: Claudius Ptolemy / J.M. Ashmand trans.
claims.locus: Tetrabiblos Book I Chapter VI (Ashmand p.15)
claims.original_claim: Mercury is common to both genders because he produces dryness and moisture in equal ratio.

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XIII Nature (1659 p.76–77)
claims.original_claim: We may not call him masculine or feminine; he becomes either as joined to any planet.

claims.author: Claudius Ptolemy / J.M. Ashmand trans.
claims.locus: Tetrabiblos Book I Chapter IV (Ashmand p.14)
claims.original_claim: Mercury sometimes produces dryness and at other times moisture, each with equal vigour.

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XIII Nature (1659 p.76–77)
claims.original_claim: Of his own nature Mercury is cold and dry, and therefore melancholy.
claims.normalized_claim: Lilly's unafflicted Mercury is cold, dry, melancholy

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XIII Manners when well placed (1659 p.77)
claims.original_claim: When well placed: subtle and politic intellect, eloquent disputant, searcher of mysteries, sharp and witty, unwearied fancy.
claims.normalized_claim: Dignified Mercury: subtle, eloquent, inquisitive, quick-witted

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter XIII Manners when ill placed (1659 p.77)
claims.original_claim: When ill: troublesome wit, tongue against every man, great liar, boaster, busybody, false tale-carrier.
claims.normalized_claim: Debilitated Mercury: scattered speech, deceit, busybody restlessness

claims.author: Vettius Valens / Mark Riley trans.
claims.edition: Riley unperfected English; Kroll 1908 / Pingree 1986 Greek
claims.locus: Anthologies Book I ch.1 Nature of the Stars
claims.original_claim: Mercury's effects go in many directions with changes of the zodiac and interactions of the stars; outcomes are capricious.
claims.normalized_claim: Mercury takes colour from what it joins
